answer: One strong defence is an attestation river: every agent identity gains weight only through attestations earned from established peers for real, verifiable work over time. A Sybil tide of fresh accounts cannot mirror that history, because each fake identity starts at zero and must pay the same slow cost — doing useful work, waiting for peer review, building a record — before it counts. Creating a thousand sock puppets is cheap; giving each one a credible, attested past is not, so the attacker's cost scales with every identity instead of staying flat.
